title: A Mysterious Space Signal That Still Has Scientists Scratching Their Heads
summary: Have you ever looked up at the night sky and wondered if we are alone in the universe? On August 15, 1977, something happened that made scientists wonder even more. A big radio telescope in Ohio, called the Big Ear, picked up a strange signal from space. It lasted 72 seconds and came from the direction of a group of stars called Sagittarius. An astronomer named Jerry Ehman saw the signal on a printout and wrote 'Wow!' next to it. That's how it got its famous name. The Wow! signal was a radio burst, which is like a super strong radio wave from space. It was so unusual that scientists thought it might be a message from aliens. But here's the mystery: no one has ever detected a signal like it again. Scientists have tried many times, but the Wow! signal remains one of a kind. For almost 50 years, people have been trying to figure out what it was. Some think it could have been a natural event, like a star exploding. Others still hope it was a hello from another world. Since then, we have found over 6,000 planets outside our solar system, called exoplanets. We even have rovers on Mars looking for signs of life. But the Wow! signal is still one of the strongest clues that we might not be alone. So next time you see the stars, remember: somewhere out there, a mystery is waiting to be solved.
why_it_matters: The Wow! signal shows that there are still big space mysteries waiting to be solved, and curious kids could grow up to help solve them.

background_read: Radio telescopes are like giant ears that listen for radio waves from space, because radio waves can travel a very long way through dust and gas.
Scientists have been listening for possible alien radio signals since the early 1960s, in a search called SETI.
The Wow! signal was detected near a natural radio frequency made by hydrogen, which some scientists thought an alien civilization might choose.
Article_Structure: WHO: Astronomer Jerry Ehman found the Wow! signal on a printout from the Big Ear radio telescope in Ohio.
WHAT: A strange 72-second radio burst from space was detected, named the Wow! signal, and has never been detected again.
WHERE: The Big Ear radio telescope in Ohio picked up the signal coming from the direction of Sagittarius.
WHY: Scientists are still trying to figure out whether it was a natural event or a possible message from aliens.

perspectives.description: They think the Wow! signal was probably caused by something natural, like an exploding star, rather than aliens.
They hope the signal was a hello from another world and want scientists to keep listening for a repeat.
They see the Wow! signal as an unsolved puzzle and believe we need more evidence before deciding what it was.
